reference: Parity scripts use OpenSSL dgst/kdf and GNU coreutils base64 as independent byte-level oracles. Contract expectations use Bash type/help behavior and published NIST SP 800-38D AES-GCM, RFC 7748 X25519, and RFC 8032 Ed25519 known-answer vectors. No expected value is derived from candidate output.
coverage: SHA-256 over empty stdin and a binary relative file, compared as raw digest bytes
SHAKE-256 with a non-default output length, compared with OpenSSL
HMAC-SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA-512 with a 257-byte key, compared with OpenSSL
RFC 5869 HKDF-SHA-256 and RFC 6070 PBKDF2-SHA-1 vectors, compared with OpenSSL KDF
Base64url unpadded encoding and padded decoding compared with GNU coreutils base64
NIST AES-GCM encryption known-answer vector and authenticated-decryption rejection
RFC 8032 Ed25519 public-key, empty-message signature, and verification vectors
exclusions: TLS connect and NTS-KE require a controlled disposable loopback TLS/ALPN peer; no network target is used.
secret-read terminal echo and prompt behavior requires a bounded disposable PTY driver.
Random key generation, Argon2id, secret-handle lifecycle, certificate parsing/signing, and other subcommands are outside this compact suite.
This suite checks bounded functional parity and published vectors; it is not cryptographic certification or security qualification.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash reports crypto as a builtin and the documented help text is available without invoking a crypto operation.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t crypto)
help_text=$(help crypto)
[[ $kind == builtin && -n $help_text ]]
printf 'builtin\nhelp-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Compare raw SHA-256 output for empty input and a deterministic binary file containing NUL and high-bit bytes; also exercise the documented file operand.
cases.script:
: > empty.bin
printf '\000A\377\n' > message.bin
if [[ $(type -t crypto) == builtin ]]; then
  crypto sha256 < empty.bin
  crypto sha256 message.bin
else
  openssl dgst -sha256 -binary < empty.bin
  openssl dgst -sha256 -binary < message.bin
fi

cases.purpose: Compare 42 raw SHAKE-256 output bytes for binary stdin, exercising a non-default XOF length.
cases.script:
printf '\000shake\377fixture' > message.bin
if [[ $(type -t crypto) == builtin ]]; then
  crypto shake256 -n 42 < message.bin
else
  openssl dgst -shake256 -xoflen 42 -binary < message.bin
fi

cases.purpose: Compare HMAC-SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA-512 on binary input with a deterministic 257-byte key, crossing the implementation's short-key allocation boundary.
cases.script:
printf '\000HMAC fixture\377' > message.bin
printf -v key '%0514d' 0
if [[ $(type -t crypto) == builtin ]]; then
  crypto hmac-sha256 -k "$key" < message.bin
  crypto hmac-sha512 -k "$key" < message.bin
else
  openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC -macopt "hexkey:$key" -binary < message.bin
  openssl dgst -sha512 -mac HMAC -macopt "hexkey:$key" -binary < message.bin
fi

cases.purpose: Compare RFC 5869 test case 1 HKDF-SHA-256 and RFC 6070 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-1 outputs byte-for-byte with OpenSSL KDF.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t crypto) == builtin ]]; then
  crypto hkdf -a sha256 -s 000102030405060708090a0b0c -k 0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b -i f0f1f2f3f4f5f6f7f8f9 -L 42
  crypto pbkdf2 -a sha1 -s 73616c74 -p password -i 1 -L 20
else
  openssl kdf -binary -keylen 42 -kdfopt digest:SHA256 -kdfopt hexkey:0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b0b -kdfopt hexsalt:000102030405060708090a0b0c -kdfopt hexinfo:f0f1f2f3f4f5f6f7f8f9 -kdfopt mode:EXTRACT_AND_EXPAND HKDF
  openssl kdf -binary -keylen 20 -kdfopt digest:SHA1 -kdfopt pass:password -kdfopt hexsalt:73616c74 -kdfopt iter:1 PBKDF2
fi

cases.purpose: Compare URL-safe unpadded encoding with GNU base64; independently supplied fixed padded text checks decoding, without feeding candidate encoding to candidate decoding.
cases.script:
printf '\373\377' > bytes.bin
if [[ $(type -t crypto) == builtin ]]; then
  encoded=$(crypto base64url -e < bytes.bin)
  printf '%s\n' "$encoded"
  printf '%s' '-_8=' | crypto base64url -d
else
  standard=$(base64 -w 0 < bytes.bin)
  url=$(printf '%s' "$standard" | tr '+/' '-_')
  url=${url%%=*}
  printf '%s\n' "$url"
  padded=$(printf '%s' "$url" | tr '_-' '/+')
  while (( ${#padded} % 4 )); do padded="${padded}="; done
  printf '%s' "$padded" | base64 --decode
fi

cases.purpose: Check AES-128-GCM encryption against the NIST SP 800-38D all-zero key, nonce, and one-block plaintext known-answer vector.
Corrupt one tag byte from the same NIST AES-GCM vector and require failure with no plaintext emitted.
cases.script:
printf '\x03\x88\xda\xce\x60\xb6\xa3\x92\xf3\x28\xc2\xb9\x71\xb2\xfe\x78\xab\x6e\x47\xd4\x2c\xec\x13\xbd\xf5\x3a\x67\xb2\x12\x57\xbd\xde' > cipher.bin
rc=0
crypto aes-gcm -d -k 00000000000000000000000000000000 -n 000000000000000000000000 < cipher.bin > clear.bin || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 && ! -s clear.bin ]]
printf 'bad-tag-rejected-without-plaintext\n'

cases.purpose: Check X25519 public-key derivation against Alice's RFC 7748 scalar/public-key vector.
Check the RFC 8032 empty-message seed/public-key/signature vector and successful signature verification.
cases.script:
: > empty.bin
seed=9d61b19deffd5a60ba844af492ec2cc44449c5697b326919703bac031cae7f60
pk=d75a980182b10ab7d54bfed3c964073a0ee172f3daa62325af021a68f707511a
sig=e5564300c360ac729086e2cc806e828a84877f1eb8e5d974d873e065224901555fb8821590a33bacc61e39701cf9b46bd25bf5f0595bbe24655141438e7a100b
crypto ed25519-pub -k "$seed" -x
crypto ed25519-sign -k "$seed" -x < empty.bin
crypto ed25519-verify -k "$pk" -s "$sig" < empty.bin
printf 'verified\n'
